uncited: The Coarse Ray Renderer (CRR) is a fast rendering technique that provides coarse density estimation and ray features for downstream processes in neural volume rendering, specifically serving the Fine Voxel Renderer (FVR) and Progressive Blur Estimation (PBE).
It builds on [Voxel-based Volume Rendering](3845-voxel-based-volume-rendering.md) by utilizing a decomposed explicit feature volume.
**Feature Aggregation:** For each point $X_i$, query the explicit feature volume $G_{coar}$ to obtain local features.
*   **Blur Handling:** When used with PBE, CRR renders color based on refined kernel locations.
Link: [Fine Voxel Renderer](3845-voxel-based-volume-rendering.md#fine-voxel-renderer) (Note: No separate article exists, so it is described here).

It differs from standard per-voxel ray casting by aggregating features along a ray and inferring color once per ray rather than querying every voxel, which significantly reduces computational cost at the expense of per-voxel accuracy [S1][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the method differs from standard per-voxel ray casting by aggregating features along a ray and inferring color once per ray, which reduces computational cost at the expense of per-voxel accuracy. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'This ray-rendering formulation has two advantages. First, it is very fast to compute; instead of querying every voxel along the ray through an MLP, Eq. (8) is only inferenced once per ray. It also serves as a coarse approximation of per-voxel rendering.' It further notes that 'CRR is used as a coarse approximation; it infers color once per ray instead of querying every voxel, which is faster but less accurate than per-voxel rendering.' Source [S2] contains identical statements regarding the speed advantage ('very fast to compute') and the trade-off ('coarse approximation', 'balance between speed and performance'). Therefore, all facts in the claim are supported by the evidence.

*   **Pitfalls:** Voxel pruning is avoided because PBE dynamically generates rays based on gradients; pruning eliminates gradients on many points and forces PBE to optimize based on small ray segments, and high-density voxels may be incorrectly estimated from blurry observations [S2, unofficial].

The claim states that voxel pruning is avoided because PBE dynamically generates rays based on gradients, pruning eliminates gradients on many points, forces PBE to optimize based on small ray segments, and high-density voxels may be incorrectly estimated from blurry observations. The provided text in Source [S2] explicitly contains the sentence: 'Importance sampling scheme is used instead of voxel pruning, as voxel pruning introduces optimization issues for PBE. Specifically... PBE dynamically generates rays rxi based on gradients from the photometric loss. In this case, voxel pruning also eliminates gradients on many points and forces PBE to optimize rxi base on small segments of the ray. Furthermore, high density voxels are often not correctly estimated from blurry observations and can lead to erroneous pruning.' This matches the claim fact-for-fact.
